text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Former Coles Myer and Just Jeans executive Peter Wilkinson has taken over as chief executive of troubled retailer David Jones Ltd, following the resignation of Chris Tideman this week. David Jones' interim results showed net profits were slashed by 50 per cent to A$22.34 million, and its first-half dividend was cut from six to four cents a share. Page 1.

Santos Ltd chief executive Ross Adler has taken large risks in the oil and gas major, however his boost in exploration spending has seen the Adelaide-based company boost profit by 77.1 per cent in 1996 to A$195.9 million, due to record production and sale levels. Adler, who has been in the position for 12 years, yesterday suggested more was to come, as he moves to inject new life into the group. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard's admission yesterday that Australia's economy needs to be growing at a rate of four to 4.5 per cent to cut the jobless rate comes amid further indications that economic activity is picking up from the 0.5 per cent seasonally adusted growth reported in the December 1996 quarter. Page 3.

A proposed A$200 million merger between St Barbara Mines NL and Mt Leyshon Gold Mines NL to create a new A$370 million gold company with operations in two States would give St Barbara some much needed capital, and Mt Leyshon a more improved exploration poential. The move indicates a further rationalisation of the gold industry. Page 17.

Following the collapse of the Adsteam empire in 1990, Tooth & Co yesterday reported an interim net profit of A$6.65 million, compared with last year's A$2.44 million loss - the company's first profit earned without the aid of abnormal asset sales. Adstea itself suffered a modest first-half loss of A$1.35 million. Page 17.

The Solomon Islands Government yesterday granted Ross Mining NL a mining lease for the A$69 million Gold Ridge mining development to proceed. The project, expected to produce one million ounces of gold in its first 10 years, goes ahead despite legal actin from landowners who alleged the current landowners' agreement goes against the country's constitution. Page 18.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Shell Australia, which controls 26 per cent of Australia's retail petrol market through 2200 service stations, looks to slash expenditure on its service station network by up to 90 per cent. Shell's massive investment in the area has returned only a one er cent profit this year, prompting a review into the company's retail operations. Page 31.

Apple Computer Australia was yesterday forced to retrench 13 per cent of its workforce as part of a global overhaul to increase profitability. As the first of the global giant's subsidiaries to suffer staff cuts, Apple Australia's remaining staff will beassigned new jobs and the company will concentrate on new markets. Page 31.

Former Coles Myer executive Peter Wilkinson, who has stepped in as David Jones Ltd chief executive, is expected to control an overhaul of the upmarket retail group's 31 stores, which may involve the closure or rebadging of marginal outlets. The review coes as David Jones yesterday reported a 50 per cent profit slump to A$22.3 million. Page 31.

An accounting ruling issued this week by the Urgent Issues Group will see companies facing a huge hit in profits over the next few years. The ruling, related to the so-called Millennium Bug which will strike on January 1, 2000, will require companies to reat billion of dollars of computer costs as bottom-line expenses. Page 31.

Despite soft advertising conditions national broadcaster Ten Group Ltd has continued its solid earnings growth with net profit before tax rising 14.6 per cent for the December half year. Ten yesterday reported a net profit of $84.9 million as advertising ales rose 17.6 per cent. The network is considering options for a $1 billion plus share market float. Page 23

Leading Australian radio executive Paul Thompson has criticised the Federal Government over delays in issuing new FM licenses - a move he says has cut competition and halted millions of dollars of industry investment. Mr Thompson - the chief executive ofDMG Radio Australia - also warned against changes to cross-media ownership rules. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Prime Minister John Howard conceded yesterday that to be able to fix Australia's unemployment problem, the Federal Government needed first to achieve unprecedented rates of growth. Howard said the economy needs to grow at around four to 4.5 per cent, resonding to fears outlined in a report by the National Institute of Labour Studies of the unemployment rate remaining around eight per cent by the end of the century. Page 29.

In a move that would most likely see Optus Communications try to integrate Optus Vision's cable network, Optus Communications is working towards a radical restructure of Optus Vision that may involve splitting the cable network from the pay television proramming operation. Page 29.

Peter Wilkinson will undertake a review of all aspects of the operations of David Jones, as he takes over as their chief executive. Wilkinson, who will leave his position as head of Just Jeans to head the upmarket retailer, has also headed Myer-Grace Bro department stores, Target, Fosseys, Katies and World 4 Kids chains. Investors had a mixed reaction to Wilkinson's appointment, which was only announced after the market closed. Page 29.

A proposed merger between St Barbara Mines and Normandy Mining's Mt Leyshon Gold Mines would see the group as Australia's ninth largest gold producer with 350,000 ounces of annual production, and 12th on a resources basis with about 4.8 million ounces in hat category with a combination of the companies' West Australian and Queensland operations. Page 29.

While Telstra advertising group manager Rod Hinchcliffe declined to identify any of the contenders in Telstra's A$100 million advertising review short list, it is understood that eleven agencies have made it to the list, including Clemenger Melbourne, Whyin TBWA, John Bevins, AIS Media, Mitchell and Partners, DDB, John Singleton Advertising, Mojo Partners, M&C Saatchi and Batey Kazoo. Page 32.

Aussie Home Loans managing director John Symond said yesterday the company's foray into business lending has shown signs of success, with over 10,000 inquiries in the month since the launch of Aussie's low interest rate mortgage-secured loans. However, te company will limit its business lending to ensure investors supplying it with funds were not spooked by an explosion of the more risky lending. Page 31.
THE AGE

After yesterday confirming a sharp drop in profits, David Jones announced one of Australia's most experienced department store executives, former Just Jeans and Myer Grace head Peter Wilkinson, will head the retailer to recovery. Wilkinson, who has also een chief operating officer for Coles Myer, will leave Just Jeans in three weeks, after being recruited by chairman and founder Craig Kimberley in late 1995. Page B1.

As 52-year old Peter Wilkinson last night celebrated his appointment to head David Jones with his family, he said would like to work for the next six to eight years until his retirement in the position. South African born Wilkinson, who ran David Jones rival Myer Grace department store group, says he believes there is a future in department stores. Page B1.

St Barbara Mines has proposed a A$334 merger deal with Normandy Mining-controlled Mount Leyshon Gold Mines that would see St Barbara bidding 32 of its shares, which trade at 80 cents, for every 10 Mount Leyshon shares (trading at A$2.10), giving an implie bid price of A$2.56 a share, adding a 22 per cent premium to the Mount Leyshon share price. Page B1.

Oil and gas group Santos has moved to a A$195.9 million profit for 1996, up by 40 per cent on 1995's A$139.9 million profit. The group has enjoyed a mix of acquisitions and exploration successes and an ability to match increased production to higher prics. Page B1.

Defiance Mills' chief executive Ian White said yesterday that Bunge's plans for a friendly takeover of the Queensland-based company are in doubt because of Bunge's plans, if successful with its A$1.70-a-share bid, to delist the public company and merge itwith Bunge's own operations. Page B2.

Food giant Goodman Fielder chief executive David Hearn told the Australian Securities Institute yesterday that the company will take another two to two-and-a-half years to become a full corporate citizen and resume franking its dividends. Hearn, who joind the group in 1995, added that this would depend on how fast the company earnings grew. Page B2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
